data.narrative:
Helios is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $26M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers in the Climate & Energy sector—including Helion, Redwood Materials, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—alongside one public comparable (Lonza, ticker LNZA). However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier characteristics to support a reliable median multiple approach.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation anchor. Using total capital raised ($26M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $52M. This method reflects the incremental value creation and dilution dynamics expected between Series A and Series B/C financing rounds in the frontier energy landscape.

Given reliance on a single applicable method, the triangulated range is centered tightly around the stage-progression result: $44M (low), $52M (median), and $60M (high). Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow peer valuation anchors—the nine same-sector comparables lack sufficient overlap in stage, tier, or metrics—and dependency on the 2.0x multiplier assumption, which may not capture Helios-specific progress, burn rate, or market conditions. Material validation would require either comparable transaction data from same-stage Climate & Energy rounds or operational metrics (revenue, unit economics, runway) not present in this dataset.
